response: Yes, it is appropriate to implant kidneys from elderly donors in young recipients. Research has shown that patient and graft survival rates for young recipients who receive kidneys from elderly donors are comparable to those who receive kidneys from young donors. However, it's worth noting that renal function tends to be better in the group of young donors. Therefore, while kidneys from elderly donors can be a viable option for young recipients, the decision should be made on a case-by-case basis, taking into account the individual circumstances and medical needs of the recipient.
